title: lean-lr, explained
h1: Logical relations, ported from Rocq to Lean: why well-typed programs behave
lead: lean-lr is Alex Bai's Lean 4 port of the logical-relations development in the MPI-SWS Semantics course. It covers the simply typed λ-calculus, System F, recursive types, mutable state, and then Iris-based relations up to concurrency. The text search finds no sorry. One caveat stands out: the contextual-refinement theorem of the ReLoC chapter takes a no-fork hypothesis that no program can satisfy, so that particular result is vacuous as stated.
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of lean-lr, Alex Bai's Lean port of the MPI-SWS Semantics course's logical relations: normalisation, parametricity, contextual equivalence, step-indexed safety with state, and Iris-based safety for a concurrent language.
startNote: Start with the smallest case: the STLC logical relation and STLC.type_safety, which (despite its name) proves that every closed well-typed term terminates. Then read the free theorem for ∀α. α → α, contextual equivalence, step-indexed safety with state, and the two Iris chapters: concurrent safety and ReLoC's refinement theorem. Read the caveat on the last one.
sizeNote: About 41,500 lines of Lean in 106 files, on Lean 4.32 and iris-lean. This site explains six headline results and the definitions they rest on, not the whole port.
agentCtx: A Lean 4 port (on iris-lean) of the MPI-SWS Semantics course's logical relations: STLC, System F, F-mu, F-mu-ref, and Iris-based unary, binary (ReLoC) and concurrent logical relations.

gloss.Nat: The natural numbers 0, 1, 2, …. Here they serve as De Bruijn indices for type variables, step indices and counts of type variables in scope.
gloss.List: A finite list. A World or a heap context is a list, and so is a thread pool.
gloss.Option: Either some x or none. A typing context lookup returns one.
gloss.String: Text. Term variables are named by strings.
gloss.Std.ExtTreeMap: A finite map (here from variable names). Typing contexts and substitutions are finite maps.
